messages:
luis: FYI we just hit a restore failure for tenant-88 during a long snapshot replay. KMS returned InvalidGrantToken while decrypting a mid-chain shard.
sec-lead: ugh. timeline? single restore or multiple tenants?
luis: single run started 1705009200, failure at ~1705009800. restore ran ~1h before failing. not a full outage but aborted and rolled back.
aj: did we recently change any RBAC or grant TTLs for the backup-operator role? I remember a change to limit ephemeral grants to 30m last month.
maria: correct — we set default ephemeral grant TTL=1800s for delegated grants issued by grantor service to reduce blast radius. That explains TTL < restore duration.
devops-sre: can we confirm from KMS/audit logs? look for CloudTrail events: `Decrypt` and `GrantToken` use. sample query: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2024-03-11T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-03-11T02:00:00Z`
aj: saw entries: `Decrypt` succeeded initially then `AccessDenied` with `InvalidGrantToken` at 1705009801. Grant create/issue shows `CreateGrant` at 1705009005 with `GrantTokens` returned. TTL shows 1800s.
sec-lead: ok that matches. So root cause: delegated grant expired mid-restore. Any other mitigations available without relaxing TTL org-wide?
maria: options: 1) increase grant TTL for this grantor service for long-running restores only, 2) change restore orchestrator to refresh grant (issue new grant) before TTL expiry, or 3) move to use IAM-based decrypt (attach decrypt permission to service principal + key policy) for restores so no ephemeral GrantToken needed.
luis: option 3 has regulatory implications for tenant isolation — we prefer not to open permanent decrypt IAM scope for multi-tenant backups.
devops-sre: short-term mitigation: re-run restore — it will create a fresh grant and likely succeed. For production we should implement refresh-on-long-run in restore controller.
aj: also consider storing envelope keys (AES) in manifest and re-wrap them server-side with a persistent CMK allowed only to backup-service; orchestrator keeps rotating ephemeral grants for decrypting AES keys. That keeps tenant isolation while avoiding single long grant.
sec-lead: we need audit trail and playbook updates. add these to encops runbook: detect InvalidGrantToken during restore -> auto-retry with reissue grant -> alert on >3 retries.
maria: note for ops: vendor KMS nuance: some providers garbage-collect unreferenced GrantTokens faster; we need to document provider TTL semantics (AWS vs GCP CMEK vs vendor HSM).
aj: action items: 1) devops-sre to implement refresh logic in restore controller (owner @devops-sre) 2) security to update runbook and RBAC policy guidance (owner @sec-lead) 3) temporary raise TTL to 2h for backup-operator grantor namespace while we ship fix (owner @maria)
devops-sre: will open PR for controller change and a canary test that simulates long-running restores.
sec-lead: I'll draft runbook changes and add detection to our monitoring (metric: restore.decrypt.invalid_grant_count).
opsbot: incident-note created: INC-20240311-88: snapshot restore failed due to expired KMS grant token; triage in progress.
luis: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with timeline and whether tenant-88 needs manual recovery.
